smells.finding: apply_delta() is 220 lines (measured by ast: scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py:425-644), comfortably a long-method smell. The diff touches it, but only to DELETE the 4-line cap-refusal branch, so it leaves the method 4 lines shorter than it found it.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md Implementation discipline: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction.' Reinforced by the g3 handoff, which scopes the gate to removing the cap and nothing else.
override.reason: The smell is pre-existing and the change strictly reduces it. Decomposing apply_delta() here would be unrequested refactoring inside a gate whose whole point is a surgical removal, and it would enlarge the diff a reviewer must reason about for the cap question. Raising it as an in-diff defect would penalize the change for a condition it improved.

smells.finding: The only class touched is the Playbook dataclass, which the diff makes SMALLER (the cap field is deleted; 5 fields remain: run_tick, dormancy_runs, apply_recurrences, apply_confirmed, ticked_work_ids + preamble/active).

The lessons-file preamble exists as TWO hand-maintained copies of the same prose, and this diff had to edit both: _default_preamble() in scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py:140-164 (seeds a playbook when none exists) and skills/workbench/templates/LESSONS.template.md (seeds one at install). The two now state the same no-cap retention story in DIFFERENT words, so they are already textually divergent and nothing checks them against each other. OBSERVATION, not a blocker: it is pre-existing structure and the diff keeps both in sync correctly (verified: neither renders a cap= header, probe_grammar.py case + grep 'cap=' skills/workbench/templates/LESSONS.template.md returns nothing).
No method in the diff reaches into another object's data. The deleted branch read book.active/book.cap from within the Playbook's own writer; removing it reduces coupling.
No repeated parameter group appears or is extended. The header fields travel as Playbook attributes, which is already the parameter object.

The playbook-state grammar is parsed with POSITIONAL regex group indices (STATE_RE at scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py:51-55, consumed as state.group(1..5) in load_playbook:236-241). This diff had to hand-renumber five of them (group(2..6) -> group(2..5)) purely because one group changed capture-ness, and an off-by-one would have silently swapped two integers rather than raising. Python's re supports named groups ((?P<dormancy_runs>\d+), state.group('dormancy_runs')), which makes the entire renumbering class impossible and would have reduced this edit to deleting one group. OBSERVATION / triage candidate, not a blocker: the renumbering as landed is CORRECT -- I verified all 16 presence combinations of the four optional fields bind to distinct sentinels, 0 failures, with a live negative control. The smell is about the next such edit, not this one.
The diff removes a constructor argument (Playbook(cap=...)) and adds none. Longest signature touched is apply_delta(book, delta) at 2 params.

One conceptual change -- 'there is no cap' -- required edits in three hand-maintained places plus six test fixtures: the writer's 8 cap sites, the writer's own _default_preamble() prose, skills/workbench/templates/LESSONS.template.md, and 6 playbook-state header string literals in tests/test_apply_lessons_delta.py that each spelled cap=20 inline. OBSERVATION, not a blocker: every site was actually caught (verified independently -- git grep -nIE '\.cap\b|DEFAULT_CAP' over scripts/ skills/ tests/ returns count=0 at HEAD against count=4 at 752a62f). The mitigation is the same one primitive-obsession names: the test fixtures spell the header as a raw literal instead of building it from the writer's own renderer, so the grammar's shape is duplicated once per fixture.
apply_lessons_delta.py changes for one reason here (the retention policy). No second, unrelated axis of change is introduced.
No chained navigation added; the diff deletes book.cap accesses rather than adding any.

Specifically hunted, because a 'tolerated' grammar field is the classic shape of it. The non-capturing (?:\s+cap=\d+)? group is NOT speculative: every lessons file in the repo carries cap=N today (.agent-work/LESSONS.md:3 confirmed), so the tolerance has a real, currently-live consumer, and the value is discarded rather than plumbed anywhere. No hook, flag, config key or extension point was added for a future cap.
A 5-line comment block (scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py:46-50) explains a 1-line regex -- superficially a comment compensating for unclear code.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md Implementation discipline: 'Match the surrounding code's naming, labeling, and in-file documentation conventions.' The file's existing convention is exactly this: TICKED_WORK_ID_RETENTION at :40-43 carries a 4-line why-comment on a single constant, and load_playbook:242-243 carries a 2-line one.
override.reason: The comment records WHY the group must stay non-capturing -- an intent that the code cannot express and that the next editor would otherwise undo by 'fixing' it into a capture group. Fowler's deodorant smell is a comment standing in for code that should be clearer; this is a decision record on a deliberate non-obvious choice, which is the sanctioned use, and it matches the in-file convention the standard requires.
